OpenAI CEO Sam Altman sits in a booth during an interview, wearing a beige sweater with a clip-on microphone.
Facebook Icon
X Icon
Reddit Icon
Comments

Email Icon
Kosta Andreadis

## What you need to know [...] Everyone's favorite tech CEO, Sam Altman, recently said that all the RAM sitting unused in personal desktop computers and laptops was a monumental waste and "quite terrible" for the world. With the current DRAM shortage and crisis, everyone's memory would be better utilized sitting in an OpenAI data center.

Go ad-free with SupporterSee plans and prices [...] This brings us to Ram-Altman, a new bash script by IainKay on GitHub that emails Sam Altman each day whenever 10% or more of your RAM is available or unused, apologizing. With messages like the following, it's a pretty funny response to the latest tone-deaf quote from Sam Altman.

Hi Sam,

Please don't be alarmed, but there is 8.6 GiB of RAM on my desk that isn't in a data center. That's 56.2% of what's installed here, and as far as I can tell it has no plans today.

Hoarding responsibly,

items.summary:
People – some of us, at least – are worried about AI eventually overthrowing human civilization. Even more immediately, there's widespread concern about the proliferation of data centers needed to support AI operations.

Yet at the same time we're collectively wringing our hands about those issues, we are meekly surrendering more and more control to machines over our everyday lives. [...] One theory about an AI Armageddon doesn't involve robots who look like Arnold Schwarzenegger hunting us down with laser guns. AI could just take over our natural habitat, as we've done with other animals and plants, which would leave us without food and shelter.

Here's a thought exercise: If AI were evaluating whether humans were worth saving for conservation purposes, would we grade out more as an invasive species or one that made important contributions to the ecosystem? [...] For that matter, we're starting to trust AI to give us authoritative answers to all of life's questions, including those where human moral judgments and lived experiences might guide us better.

After all, why bother doing any research on our own when we can just type a question into a search field and have some chatbot spit out a near-instantaneous response?

items.title: GPT-5 Shows Substantial Agreement in Interpreting Ultrasound Cochrane
items.summary: When compared to the consensus reference standard, GPT-5 demonstrated varying levels of agreement across the different variables. The model showed the highest agreement for review purpose, with 88.9% exact agreement and a Cohen’s kappa of 0.793. For evidence certainty, the model achieved 70.4% exact agreement, with a quadratic weighted kappa of 0.782, indicating substantial agreement when accounting for the ordinal nature of the certainty scale. [...] A new descriptive meta-research study published in BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making evaluates the performance of the GPT-5 API in structurally interpreting ultrasound-related Cochrane reviews. The research, conducted by a team including Weizao Wu, Anchen Liu, and colleagues, aims to clarify the role of ultrasound within systematic reviews and assess the field-specific capabilities of large language models in evidence synthesis. By combining a two-level analysis of review topics with [...] To evaluate the GPT-5 API, the researchers employed a structured extraction process targeting four key variables: review purpose, clinical domain, evidence certainty, and conclusion polarity. Two independent clinicians annotated the focused subset of 54 reviews while blinded to the GPT-5 outputs. Disagreements between the human reviewers were resolved through consensus adjudication, creating a final operational reference standard against which the AI’s performance was measured.

items.title: Study Finds Lower Unaided Scores After Brief Tasks With GPT-5 Access | TokenPost
items.summary:
Access to GPT-5 helped participants during short math and reading tasks, but groups offered the tool scored lower on unaided questions immediately afterward in three randomized experiments involving U.S.-based participants.

The experiments recruited 1,222 people: 354 for the first fraction test, 667 for the second and 201 for the reading test. After exclusions, the analyses included 305, 585 and 168 participants, respectively. [...] During sessions lasting about 10 to 15 minutes, GPT-5 was available beside the questions and could provide complete solutions. Scores improved while the assistant was available. Researchers removed access before the final three questions in each experiment, then measured how participants performed without it. [...] The second fraction experiment found a smaller accuracy gap. Participants previously offered GPT-5 answered 71% of the final questions correctly, compared with 77% for the control group. Skip rates were 10% and 7%, respectively, but that difference was not statistically significant in the full comparison.

items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary:
Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”

The approach centers on a brain-like embodied large model as the intelligence core, mass-producible and stable robotic bodies as the vehicle, and real-world productivity scenarios as the driving force. [...] Gasgoo Munich-On November 9, AI² Robotics announced it has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Danantara Development Management Fund (DDMF), the investment arm of Indonesia's state-backed wealth fund Danantara Indonesia. The partnership will focus on pilot applications, industrial collaboration, and local deployment of general-purpose intelligent robots and embodied AI technology across the archipelago. [...] The agreement was signed during the inaugural Danantara Technology Innovation Investment Forum (DTIIF 2026) in Jakarta, with Zhang Peng, AI² Robotics's co-founder, signing on behalf of the company.

Image Credit: AI² Robotics

Operating independently under the president's office, Danantara Indonesia holds substantial influence. AI² Robotics is now the first—and currently the only—robotics company to join DDMF's embodied AI cooperation roster.

items.title: ListEasier introduces AI robotics for automated e-commerce listings
items.summary:
Find out more

Under the system, robotics hardware places items, captures images from several angles using computer vision and records spatial dimensions without manual intervention.

ListEasier’s vision and natural language processing models then analyse the visual data, extract product attributes, identify condition details and generate listing metadata. [...] Its PriceEasier engine calculates price points across global marketplaces, while completed catalogue profiles are sent to sales channels and marketplaces in seconds.

ListEasier said the launch covers warehouse automation, industrial reverse logistics and high-volume e-commerce inventory processing, segments it estimates represent a C$45bn (US$31.89bn) total addressable market.

The system is designed to reduce manual labour requirements and inspection delays in listing workflows, it added. [...] The launch follows the company’s reported milestone of listing more than $200m in gross merchandise value and a sixfold increase in data-processing speed.

ListEasier co-founder and COO Josh van der Meulen said: “Transitioning AI out of the browser and directly onto the warehouse floor represents a structural shift in inventory processing. We are turning manual physical inventory intake into a high-speed, automated assembly line.”

items.title: Kenwood High School JROTC Robotics Program earns regional recognition - ClarksvilleNow.com
items.summary:
“I am proud of the national-level success of Kenwood’s Robotics Team. It reflects the faculty, JROTC instructors, and cadets’ hard work and dedication toward creating an elite mindset at the school,” Lightner said.

Dr Nigel Anderson, Kenwood High School Principal, noted “The robotics program complements the leadership development and citizenship training provided through JROTC while exposing students to science, technology, engineering, and mathematics disciplines.” [...] CLARKSVILLE TN – The Kenwood High School JROTC Robotics Program has grown from a single robotics team into a four-team program that is competing successfully at regional and national-level events. The program currently fields Teams 26163X, 26163A, 26163L, and 26163S, providing students with opportunities to develop skills in engineering, programming, and problem-solving. [...] During the current robotics’ competition season, Team 26163X captured first place at the Tennessee State Fair Robotics Competition. The team followed that performance with another first-place finish at a competition in Elizabethton, Tennessee, where it also received a technical award recognizing excellence in robot design and engineering.
